messages.subject: Re: Control jitter for overlaying plots
parts:
You can do that, but it won't work if you're using a discrete variable. For example, if your x variable is a factor, you can't pre-jitter that column of your data.

-Winston


On Mon, Jan 7, 2013 at 10:54 AM, kgoldfeld <kgol...@gmail.com> wrote:
I am trying to overlay two different shapes on points that I am plotting - but I am using a position_jitter option in generating the first plot.  Of course, when I try to overlay the new shape, the jitter creates another random position, so the overlay does not work.  I was wondering if I can "control" the jitter a bit by using the R "jitter" function outside of ggplot, and have the position argument in geom_point use that information.

--

messages.author: ab3857f95c4d14eb
messages.subject: Re: Control jitter for overlaying plots
parts:
Thanks Winston.  I was able to something working with discrete data.  Here is some code that provides an example of a plot.  There may be a more elegant way to do this, but it this works:

x=rbinom(100,1,.5)
y=rnorm(100,50,5)
z=rbinom(100,1,.2)

j.x = jitter(x,factor=.2) + 1
j.xz = ifelse(z,j.x,NA)

testdat = data.frame(x,y,j.x,j.xz)
dummy = data.frame(x=c(0,1),y=c(50,60),grp=c(1,1))
              
ggplot(data=testdat) +
  geom_point(aes(x=j.x,y=y),colour="blue",size=2,shape=19) + # Plot all x's (jittered)
  geom_point(aes(x=j.xz,y=y),colour="red",size=4,shape=1) +  # Circle x's with z=1 (same jitter)
  geom_path(data=dummy,aes(x=factor(x),y=y,group=grp),linetype=0) + # Forces the x-axis to only 2 factors
  scale_y_continuous() +
  scale_x_discrete()
